title: Customer evidence digest and closure flow
content:
TL;DR:
On 2026-10-30 we observed an intermittent degradation affecting streaming completions for a subset of tenant workloads in eu-west-1. Root cause: a cascading eviction pattern in the runtime cache layer triggered during a poorly timed autoscaler activity, which increased cold-kernel invocations and led to elevated tail latency and some truncated streams. No customer data was exfiltrated; integrity of stored inputs/outputs is intact.

Customer-facing summary (one paragraph):
We experienced elevated streaming latency and occasional truncated responses for some customers in EU-West on 2026-10-30 between 09:12–11:07 UTC. We fixed the immediate condition at 10:45 UTC by rolling a config patch to reduce aggressive cache eviction during scaling; a follow-up kernel alignment deploy completed at 11:07 UTC. If you saw partial or truncated responses, please follow the verification steps below — we have replay and verification options available. We apologize for the disruption; we recognize the impact and are offering targeted replay assistance where needed.

Impact scope:
- Affected region: eu-west-1 (primary) with transient cross-region retries on affected requests.
- Symptoms: increased 95th/99th latency for streaming responses, intermittent truncation, and a small number of duplicate fragments for long-running sessions.
- Customers affected: approximate 0.6% of accounts had measurable impact (high-traffic tenants with long sequence lengths).
- Data integrity: no loss or corruption detected in persisted artifacts.

Customer verification steps (actionable):
1) Check your recent response IDs: if you have response IDs from 2026-10-30 09:00–12:00 UTC, open a support ticket with a sample of 3 response IDs and we will run a proof-of-integrity check.
2) For truncated outputs: request a targeted replay of the affected request batch — our team can re-run those inputs against the same model/commit with previous KV cache snapshot and provide full outputs.
3) For duplicate fragments: provide the session ID and sequence offsets; we will correlate logs and provide an artifact with the ordered token stream plus checksums.

Evidence digest we will provide (what CS will attach to customer replies):
- Per-request timing and kernel invocation histogram for each supplied response ID.
- KV cache eviction timeline excerpt for impacted host(s) (redacted host identifiers).
- Checksums (SHA256) of stored outputs and the replayed outputs to show exact match / divergence.
- Short transcript of our remediation steps and timestamps (human-readable).

Closure decision flow (customer-facing choices):
A) Verify and close: customer confirms they saw no functional regression after replay or confirms outputs acceptable -> close incident and optional credit.
B) Request replay assistance: we perform targeted replays and provide artifacts; if outputs differ materially, we offer options (manual rerun, batch regeneration, or file-level reconciliation).
C) Request SLA credit / remediation: if customer elects, CS will escalate to account team for compensation review (apply SLA policy).

Suggested customer email template (short):
Hi <Customer Name>,

We’re reaching out about elevated streaming latency and truncated responses you may have seen on 2026-10-30 in eu-west-1. We’ve fixed the platform issue and can replay any affected requests and provide integrity proofs (checksums + logs). If you’d like us to investigate specific response IDs, reply with up to three examples and we’ll prioritize.

Thanks,
<Redwood CS rep>

Internal notes for CS (do not send to customers):
- Priority for replays: enterprise tenants flagged in account healthboards -> then higher-RPS API keys.
- Use support tag: inc-4821-evidence. Include linked_artifacts URLs and attach the kernel/hypervisor excerpts.
- Engineering contact: Priya Menon (applied-ml) for replay orchestration; Jordan Blake (serving-runtime) for kernel-level trace clarifications.

Post-incident mitigations (what we will tell customers we are doing):
- Short term: keep new cache eviction safety knob enabled for 72 hours in eu-west-1 and to be toggled during scheduled autoscaler windows.
- Mid term: add a sequencing guard to the autoscaler to prevent eviction bursts during bursty scale-ups; ETA: 3 weeks.
- Long term: improved cold-kernel warmup heuristics and per-tenant eviction thresholds; ETA: 8–10 weeks, prioritized for tenants with long-context workloads.

Next steps and timeline for customer-facing postmortem:
- 2026-11-02: publish this customer-facing summary and open support triage for replays.
- 2026-11-09: publish detailed technical postmortem (confluence) with anonymized telemetry.
- 2026-11-30: follow-up with final remediation status and SLA decisions where applicable.

Contact and escalation: reply to this thread or open a support case and include tag inc-4821-evidence. For immediate escalation, CC your account lead and copy eng-oncall at eng-oncall@redwood.ai.

[CS TODO checklist]
- Attach evidence artifacts to ticket (timings + checksums)
- Offer replay option in first response
- Log customer choice in incident tracker (close / replay / compensation)
- If compensation requested, route to finance+legal for approval

End of draft.
